task.name.empty: The task name cannot be empty.
task.name.windows: The task name `{name}` does not work on Windows: the task name is the folder name. Use none of `< > : " | ? *`, and do not end with a space or a dot.
task.name.bad: The task name `{name}` cannot be used. No `/` or `\`, no `.` at the start, {limit} characters at most.
task.exists: Task `{task}` exists already. To go on with it, run `{command} task open {name} --session-id <session id>`.
task.missing: There is no task `{name}`. See which there are: `{command} task list --all`. To make one: `{command} task new {name} --kind <kind> --session-id <session id>`.
task.session.missing: There is no session `{session_id}`. Use the "current session id" from the rules at the top of this prompt, copied as written.
task.session.subagent: A subagent cannot open a task or switch tasks.
task.session.admin: This session is in admin mode and cannot work on a task. Ask the user to open another conversation, or to run `admin off` first.
task.closed: Task `{task}` is closed. To go on with it, run `{command} task open {name} --session-id <session id>`.
task.upgrade.down: The task is at the "{current}" tier and cannot change to "{wanted}". A tier only goes up, never down.
task.upgrade.same: The task is at the "{current}" tier already.
task.next.light: Read {task}/TASK.md first. Do the work, then write the result and the next step back into TASK.md.
task.next.medium: Read {task}/TASK.md first, then REQ.md, REQ/ and REF/. Write the requirement as you understand it into {task}/REQ.md and ask the user to look at it; when the requirement changes, change that file. Results go at the root of {task}/ (for example RCA.md, DESIGN.md). Append what you did, and why, to LOG.md. Update TASK.md before you stop.
task.next.full: Read {task}/TASK.md first, then REQ.md, REQ/ and REF/. Write the requirement as you understand it into {task}/REQ.md and ask the user to look at it; when the requirement changes, change that file. Write the steps into TODO.md. Update TASK.md before you stop, and append the decisions you made to LOG.md.
task.next.switched: This session was on `{other}` before; that task is still open, not closed. To go back: `{command} task open {other_name} --session-id <session id>`.
task.waiting.plan: the plan waits for your approval
task.waiting.promote: the write-back waits for your approval
task.waiting.recover: the promote failed halfway and waits for you to recover
task.upgrade.done: Raised to the "{tier}" tier. Change the tier line in {task}/TASK.md to "{tier}".
task.relay.reminder: In this round you wrote files in the task folder {task} but did not update {task}/TASK.md. Update it now: status, doing now, next step, decided. Change this one file only, then end. It is the handover file the next session reads.
task.inject.head: Task: {task} ({kind}, {tier} tier), round {round}. A new session reads {task}/TASK.md first, then what it points to; update it before you stop.
task.inject.scope: The edit tools can write this task folder only: the requirement goes in REQ.md, results that are not written back go at the root, results to write back go in {task}/DEV/ (after the plan is approved); REQ/ and REF/ hold the user's material and are read only. A target repository is written only with `{command} task promote`: --dry-run first, then the user approves in the terminal. Only the user can run approve-plan, approve-promote and recover. Do not clean up files with `rm`. The task folder is ignored by git, so search tools such as Glob and Grep do not find the files in it: read them by path with the file-reading tool, or use `ls` in the terminal.
task.inject.board: The task's page, where the user follows it (plan, TODO, log, changes, approvals): {url}. This is the task's URL: give it when the user asks for the link or the page of the task, and with the path whenever you point at a task file. Never open or request it yourself: the gate refuses.
rules.task.entry: When the user asks you to produce or change files (RCA, design, plan, development, tests, knowledge base changes), or mentions going on with, continuing or looking at an existing task (even just to ask how far it is), first open or pick up the task with the skill `harness-my-task`, then read, then act. For plain Q&A that writes nothing and touches no existing task, do not. Without a task you cannot call the reviewer; the mapper does not depend on a task, only on whether the user typed `/generic-mapreduce`. The files of a target repository are never changed directly.
gate.target.direct: `{repo}/{relative}` is in the working tree of the target repository {repo}. A target repository is never changed directly: only promote writes to it. Change `DEV/{repo}/{relative}` in the task folder, then write it back with `{command} task promote` (the user must approve). If the repository already has this file, fetch it first: `{command} task fetch {repo}/{relative}`. If there is no task yet, open one with the skill `harness-my-task`.
review.off: Independent checks are off for this task. They run only when the user writes `[review]=n` in a prompt (n is the number of passes needed in a row). Do not switch them on yourself, and do not call the reviewer.
review.nothing: Task {task} has no work to check yet. Write the work first (under DEV/ if it is written back, at the root of the task folder if not), then run `{command} task review start`.
review.enough: The passes needed in a row ({n}) are reached: no more checks are needed. A new check is needed only when the work changes.
review.limit: The checks are used up: checks done: {used}; limit: {limit}; and there are not enough passes yet. Stop: do not change or check any more. Tell the user where the last problems are (the newest verdict.md under {task}/REVIEW/) and ask the user to decide: run `{command} task review extend --checks <number>` in their own terminal for more checks, or `{command} task review waive` to stop checking. You cannot run these two commands.
review.start.next: Now call the subagent `{agent}`. The call message is one sentence only: "Check the review package {package}". Do not write your reasoning, your conclusion, or what you think is fine. After it answers, the verdict is saved as verdict.md in the same folder by itself. Then run `{command} task review status` for the next step.
review.next.waived: The user has waived the checks: no more are needed.
review.next.done: The passes needed in a row ({n}) are reached. You may go on.
review.next.more: Passes still needed: {left} (needed in a row: {n}, each with a new reviewer). Run `{command} task review start`.
review.next.fix: The last check did not pass. Read {verdict} and fix the work as it says; then run `{command} task review start` to check again. Passes still needed: {left}.
review.package.title: # Review package: {name}, check {number}
review.package.first: This is check 1. Do a full check.
review.package.later: This is check {ordinal} (the 2nd or later). Still do a full check, but **report only what affects correctness**: wording, format, naming and nicer ways to write something are not reported.
review.package.unconfirmed: The confirmation line of {req} is not filled in yet. Only the user can change that line; the author cannot. **It is not a problem: do not give FAIL for it.** Treat the requirement as "to be confirmed": check against what REQ.md says now.
review.package.diff:
## Diff

The diff between the work and main is in {path}. Read it first; for a large file read only the diff and the lines around it. The work is not in a git repository: do not use git diff.
review.package.previous:
## The problems of the last check

The last check did not pass; its text is in {path}. First confirm, one by one, whether each is fixed, then do the full check.
review.package.output:
## How to answer

The first line is `VERDICT: PASS` or `VERDICT: FAIL`. After it, one line per finding: `- <file>:<line> <what does not match> | basis: <source>`. A finding with no file and line does not count.
review.extend.screen: Task {task}: checks done: {used}; limit: {limit}; last verdict: {last}. More checks to give: {checks}.
review.extend.next: Tell the agent it may go on checking.
review.waive.screen: Task {task}: passes needed in a row: {n}; passes so far: {passes}; checks done: {used}; last verdict: {last}. After the waiver this version of the work can be promoted with no more checks. If the work changes, the waiver ends.
review.waive.ask: To stop checking and let this version through
review.waive.next: Tell the agent the checks are waived and it may run task promote --dry-run.
review.waive.unneeded: No waiver is needed: checks are off for this task, or it has enough passes already.
review.waive.changed: The work changed while you were confirming. Run this command again.
review.promote.refused: It cannot be written back yet: independent check passes needed in a row: {n}; so far: {passes}.
review.call.other: With a task, only the subagent `{agent}` can be called (you called: {called}), and a check must be started first.
review.call.no_round: Before calling `{agent}`, run `{command} task review start`: it saves this version of the work and writes the review package. Then call it.
review.stop: Independent checks are on for task {task}, and this version of the work does not have enough passes yet. {next}
review.inject: Independent checks: passes needed in a row: {n} (`[review]={n}`); passes so far: {passes}; checks done: {used}; limit: {limit}. When the work is written: `{command} task review start`, then call `{agent}`; if it does not pass, fix it as verdict.md says and check again; only with enough passes can you run `task promote --dry-run`.
review.start.context: The review package of this check: {package}. Read it first and check as it says. Your answer is saved as written, as verdict.md in the same folder.
rules.task.open_list: Tasks that are not closed ({count}): {names}. When the user means one of them, first run `{command} task open <task name> --session-id <current session id>` to pick it up, then read its TASK.md. If you read or write without picking it up, the rules do not apply.
task.inject.req: When what the user asks in this prompt differs from {task}/REQ.md, or adds a new condition: change REQ.md first and add a line to its change record, then touch the work. A direct instruction ("write it as ...", "add a sentence ...") is a change of the requirement too. An independent check goes by REQ.md only.
rules.session: Current session id: {session_id}. Use it as written for --session-id of `{command} task new` and `task open`. When a tool call is refused, do the next step the refusal gives; do not look for another way around.
rules.review.no_task: The user wrote `[review]={n}` in this prompt: an independent check is wanted. A check needs a task. First open or pick up a task with the skill `harness-my-task` (the light tier is enough for something simple); n is carried into the task by itself.
rules.subagent.no_task: This session has no task, so it cannot call a subagent (you called: {called}). Do the work yourself. For an independent check: first open or pick up a task with the skill `harness-my-task`; `{agent}` can be called only after the user writes `[review]=n`.
rules.subagent.admin: Admin mode allows no subagent (you called: {called}). Do the work yourself.
mapreduce.call.not_asked: The subagent `{agent}` cannot be called: it is available only after the user types `/{skill}` (and again after it is used up or out of date). You cannot switch it on yourself. Do the work yourself; if running in parallel seems worth it, tell the user they can type `/{skill}`, and say roughly how much more it costs.
mapreduce.call.limit: The {limit} calls of `{agent}` for this `/{skill}` are used up: no more are sent. Finish with the summaries you have; if they really are not enough, tell the user which parts are missing, and the user decides whether to type `/{skill}` once more.
mapreduce.start.context: You are a mapper: read only, change no file, run no command. Do only the part the call message gives you. When you have read it, hand in a summary only: conclusions first, each with its source (file path and line number), and at the end "not found" and "not sure". Do not paste long passages.
rules.admin:
Admin mode: on (the user approved it in their own terminal). This session is for extending and debugging the harness.
You may change the files of the harness, guardrail files included. Still closed: {locked} (read only), files the CLI writes (reports, a task's `.task/` and so on), `.git`, target repositories.
You cannot call a subagent or open a task. Only the user can run the approval commands (approve-plan, approve-promote, recover, approve-command, admin on, task review extend, task review waive). The rules for git write commands and dangerous commands stay the same.
After changing `.harness/engine/`, a policy or the hook configuration, run `{command} doctor` and the tests, and hand over to the user only when both pass. When a tool call is refused, do the next step the refusal gives.
Current session id: {session_id}. When you are done, remind the user to run `{command} admin off --session-id {session_id}`.
task.waiting.review: the checks are used up and wait for your decision
task.waiting.go-plan: the plan is approved: tell the agent to go on
task.waiting.go-promote: the write-back is approved: tell the agent to run it
task.waiting.go-recover: the repositories are put back: tell the agent to try again
task.waiting.go-review: the checks are decided: tell the agent to go on
desk.wait.go-recover: The agent does not know yet: nothing tells it. In VS Code, send it a message, for example:
desk.wait.go-review: The agent does not know yet: nothing tells it. In VS Code, send it a message, for example:
desk.go.recover: The repositories are put back. Try the write-back again.
desk.go.review: The checks are decided. Go on.
task.waiting.stopped: the agent stopped and waits for you
task.waiting.cancelled: you cancelled the agent; it waits for you
task.waiting.autorun: autorun stopped and waits for you
autorun.inject: Autorun is on (pushed on {step}/{limit} times so far): work down {task}/TODO.md, tick each step when it is done, write decisions and reasons into LOG.md, and do not stop to ask the user. No promote on the way. When you cannot go on, run `{command} task autorun off --reason "<why>"`, then stop.
autorun.next.step: Go on with the next unticked step in {task}/TODO.md: "{step}" ({left} steps left). When it is done, tick it in TODO.md, update TASK.md, and write your decisions and reasons into LOG.md. Do not ask the user, and do not promote. When you cannot go on (missing information, a trade-off the plan does not cover, a refusal), run `{command} task autorun off --reason "<why>"`, then stop.
autorun.next.review: Every step is ticked, and the independent check has not passed yet. {next}
autorun.next.promote: Every step is ticked and the check has passed. Run `{command} task promote --dry-run`, put the link to PROMOTE-PLAN.diff in your answer, then stop and wait for the user to approve. Do not run promote without --dry-run.
autorun.cannot: Autorun cannot be switched on now:
autorun.need.plan: There is no plan yet. Let the agent write PLAN.md first, then run `{command} task approve-plan --task {name}`.
autorun.need.approval: The plan is not approved, or it changed after the approval. Run `{command} task approve-plan --task {name}` first.
autorun.need.todo: {task}/TODO.md has no unticked step. Let the agent break the work into `- [ ] step` lines there first (for a light or medium task, run `{command} task upgrade --tier full` first).
autorun.need.review: Independent checks are off for this task. With nobody watching there must be a reviewer: first send a prompt with `[review]=1` in the session of the task.
autorun.need.round: This round was written back already, or the write-back failed halfway. To do more, open a new round or recover first.
autorun.changed: While you were confirming, the plan or the steps changed, or a condition no longer holds. Not switched on. Run it again to see the new content.
autorun.screen.head: Task {task} (round {round}): switch autorun on (beta). The agent works down TODO.md and no longer stops after each step to wait for you.
autorun.screen.limits: When it stops: pushed on {steps} times; {minutes} minutes passed; refusals by the gate: {denies}; several rounds with no progress; the independent check ([review]={n}) has used its checks ({checks}) without a pass; the plan changes; the agent says it cannot go on.
autorun.screen.scope: Scope: it can write {task}/ only, and the plan is the version you approved. git and the target repositories stay out of reach as before.
autorun.screen.end: When it is done: it makes the write-back plan and stops. The write-back still needs your approve-promote. You can switch it off any time with `task autorun off`.
autorun.screen.question: To switch autorun on
autorun.on.next: Autorun is on. Go back to the session of the task and send "start". After that you need not watch; for progress: `{command} task list --watch` or `{command} task autorun status`.
autorun.off.reason: Switching autorun off needs a reason: `{command} task autorun off --reason "<why it cannot go on>"`. The user reads it to see where it got stuck.
autorun.off.next.person: Autorun is off. The next time the agent stops, it is not pushed on any more.
autorun.off.next.agent: Autorun is off, and the reason is recorded. Stop now, and tell the user in a sentence or two where it got stuck and what they need to decide.
autorun.why.done: done: every step is ticked, the check passed, and the write-back plan is made (or there is nothing to write back)
autorun.why.plan: the plan is no longer the approved version
autorun.why.review: the independent checks are used up without a pass
autorun.why.denied: refusals by the gate reached the limit
autorun.why.steps: the times pushed on reached the limit
autorun.why.agent: the agent said it cannot go on
task.pause.next: The task is paused: the board no longer says it waits for you, and this time does not count as waiting. To go on: `{command} task resume --task {name}`, or just send a prompt in its session.
task.pause.already: Task {name} is paused already. To go on: `{command} task resume --task {name}`.
task.resume.not_paused: Task {name} is not paused: nothing to resume.
insight.not_started: Task `{task}` has not started: there is no record to analyse.
insight.wait.reply: the agent stopped and waited for your reply
insight.wait.cancelled: you cancelled the agent; it waited for you
insight.wait.plan: waiting for you to approve the plan
insight.wait.promote: waiting for you to approve the write-back
insight.wait.review: the checks were used up, waiting for your decision
insight.wait.recover: waiting for you to recover the repository
insight.why.calls: It made {calls} tool calls in all
insight.why.part: Of that, "{part}" took {time} ({turns} turns, {calls} tool calls)
insight.finding.waiting: Waiting for you took {waiting}; the agent worked for {active}: waiting is {share} of the whole. The longest wait came after prompt {prompt}: {longest} ({reason}).
insight.finding.slow_prompt: The slowest was prompt {prompt}: {time}, {share} of the working time. {why}.
insight.finding.time_split: Of the working time, the biggest part is "{part}": {time}, {share}.
insight.finding.approval: Tools stopped to wait for your confirmation click for {time} in all, {share} of the working time.

insight.finding.context: The context grew from {first} tokens to {largest} tokens ({times} times). The larger the context, the more each later turn costs.
insight.finding.tool_results: Tool {tool}: {calls} calls. Its results came to {tokens} tokens, all of which went into the context.
insight.finding.slow_tool: The tool that took the most time is {tool}: {calls} calls, {time} in all, {longest} for the longest.
insight.finding.refused: Actions the hook refused: {denied}. Times it blocked Stop: {blocks}. After each refusal the agent has to try another way.
insight.finding.no_usage: For some sessions Copilot's session record was not found: that part has times only, no usage.
insight.finding.paused: You paused this task for {time} (`task pause`). That time does not count as "waiting for you".

gate.guardrail.file: `{relative}` is a guardrail file ({pattern}). It cannot be changed. Do not change it, and do not get around this with a terminal command. If it must change, stop and tell the user what to change: the user changes it, or switches to the admin agent.
gate.admin.file: `{relative}` cannot be changed in admin mode either ({pattern}): session state, approval records and logs live here, read only. Do not get around this with a terminal command. If it really must be cleaned or repaired, stop and tell the user: the user does it.
gate.admin.terminal: This terminal command would change files that stay closed in admin mode too ({why}), such as the session state, approval records and logs in `.harness/runtime/`. Do not retry with another command. If it really must be cleaned or repaired, stop and tell the user: the user does it.
gate.guardrail.terminal: This terminal command would change a guardrail file ({why}). Guardrail files cannot be changed. Do not retry with another command. If it must change, stop and tell the user what to change: the user changes it, or switches to the admin agent.
gate.git_folder.file: `{shown}` is inside a `.git` folder. `.git` is never changed directly: that breaks the history and the settings of the repository. Do not change it, and do not get around this with a terminal command. If you need a commit or another branch, stop and tell the user.
gate.git_folder.terminal: This terminal command would directly change a `.git` folder or a path a target repository refuses ({why}). Do not retry with another command. If it is needed, stop and tell the user what to do: the user does it.
gate.target.refused: `{repo}/{relative}` is a path the target repository {repo} refuses ({pattern}, see refused_paths in target.json). It is never changed. If it must change, stop and tell the user: the user changes it.
gate.target.terminal: This terminal command would directly change files in the working tree of a target repository ({why}). Only promote writes to a target repository. Do not retry with another command. Fetch the file into the task's DEV/, change it there, then write it back with promote.
gate.task.plan_req: `{relative}` is under the task's `DEV/`. The requirement of the task changed after the user approved the plan, so `DEV/` is closed again. Check that {task}/PLAN.md still fits the requirement (change it if not), then stop and tell the user to read the requirement and the plan again, confirm the requirement and run `{command} task approve-plan` (or press the buttons on the task's page). Go on when the user says it is approved. Work that is not written back (RCA, design, notes) goes at the root of {task}/ meanwhile.
desk.req.changed: The requirement changed after you confirmed it or after you approved the plan. Read it again: confirm it, and approve the plan again.
gate.task.plan_first: `{relative}` is under the task's `DEV/`. `DEV/` can be written only after the user approves the plan (it is not approved now, or it changed after the approval). Write [PLAN.md]({task}/PLAN.md), then stop and ask the user to run `{command} task approve-plan` in their own terminal. Go on when the user says it is approved. Work that is not written back (RCA, design, notes) needs no approval: write it at the root of `{task}/`.
gate.task.outside: Task {task} is open: you may write only inside the task folder `{task}/`, and you tried to write `{relative}`. Work that is not written back (RCA, design, notes) goes at the root of the task folder; work to write back to a target repository goes under `{task}/DEV/<repository>/<path>`.
gate.task.person_files: `{relative}` is in `REQ/` or `REF/` of task {task}. Those hold the user's material and are read only. Write notes and results at the root of the task folder `{task}/`.
gate.board.request: Refused: this asks the board server on port {port}, and its buttons are the user's. Do not call it. If something on the board should change, tell the user.
gate.terminal.denied: This terminal command is refused: {why}. Do not retry with a command of the same kind. If it is needed, stop and tell the user why: the user runs it.
gate.terminal.ask: The user must confirm this terminal command: {why}.
gate.cli_owned.file: `{relative}` is written and updated by the CLI. It cannot be written directly. Change it with a `{command}` command; if there is no such command, stop and tell the user.
gate.cli_owned.terminal: This terminal command would directly change files the CLI writes ({why}), such as a task's `.task/`, `REVIEW/`, `SNAPSHOT/` and the reports. Change them with a `{command}` command; if there is no such command, stop and tell the user.
gate.git.never:
This git command can never be approved: {why}. Command: {git_command}
Do not retry with another spelling. If it is needed, stop and tell the user why: the user runs it in their own terminal.
gate.git.why.push: it sends commits to the remote repository
gate.git.why.update-ref: it moves a branch or deletes a ref directly
gate.git.why.prune: it deletes unreferenced objects for good

task.step.plan: Read REQ/, REF/ and the knowledge base. To change a target repository: write the plan to {plan} (which files change, how, and how to accept the result), then stop, give the user the link [PLAN.md]({plan}), and ask the user to run `{command} task approve-plan` in their own terminal; {dev}/ cannot be written before the approval. Work that does not change a target repository (RCA, design, notes) needs no plan: write it at the root of {task}/. When the result is written and the "Done when" of REQ.md are met, ask the user whether to close the task, and run `{command} task close` only after they say yes: closing writes the report and lets the session go, and the user may still have questions. If the change renames or removes something other code may use (a table, a column, a procedure, a job), run the skill generic-impact-analysis before you write the plan.
task.step.page: The user reads the plan on the task's page: {url}. Give that address with the link.
task.step.approve: The user has not approved the plan yet (or it, or the requirement, changed after the approval). Give the user the link [PLAN.md]({plan}) and ask the user to run `{command} task approve-plan` in their own terminal. {dev}/ cannot be written before the approval; work that is not written back can go at the root of {task}/ meanwhile.
task.step.approved: The plan is approved. Work to write back to a target repository goes under {dev}/<repository>/<path>; work that is not written back (RCA, design, one-off scripts) goes at the root of {task}/.
task.step.fetch: To change a file the repository already has, fetch it first with `task fetch <repository>/<path>`; when done, run `task diff`, then `task promote --dry-run`.
task.step.close: When everything is done, run `task close`. Then give the user the report link and say that `/harness-task-report` explains where the time and usage went. If the task taught something a future agent would miss, or `LOG.md` notes knowledge base cards that are wrong, stale or missing (not a defect of the harness or the toolkit: tell the user about those), name them in two or three lines and ask the user whether to run the skill generic-capture-knowledge; do not run it unasked.
task.step.standards: The company has code standards plugged in (.harness/standards/code-standards.md). If this task changed code, ask the user whether to run the skill generic-code-standards before `task diff`; do not run it unasked.

kbmap.next: Use `kb near <id>` for what one object uses and what uses it, and `kb split` for a first cut of the domains. `missing`: names used but defined nowhere in the repositories (deleted, or never committed); `obsolete_used`: retired code still in use. `dynamic` objects run code known only at run time: read them, or ask the user, before you rely on their uses. `unresolved`: names that fit no object (aliases, or a form the toolkit misreads). How right the map is: `kb audit` (generic-kb-toolkit-audit).
kbmap.next.facts: Check `facts` first: the toolkit does not yet find every use the person knows (or there is no facts.jsonl). Look also at `empty_files` and `failed_files`. Until they are right, the map misses uses: fix the toolkit (/generic-kb-toolkit-build).

kbmap.none: There is no map yet. Run `kb map` first.
kbmap.near.none: No object in the map is called `{query}`. Run `kb map` again if the code changed.
kbmap.near.many: More than one object fits. Ask again with one of these ids.
kbmap.near.dynamic: This object runs SQL known only at run time: the uses listed may be incomplete.
kbmap.split.next: A first cut, by script: entry points joined by what they use. `shared` objects are used from many entry points and belong in shared/. Write the proposal for the user, with names they would use; the user confirms the domains once.
kbmap.split.one_big: One domain holds {size} objects: something used everywhere still joins them. Try a lower `--shared-min` (now {limit}).
kbstatus.audit.old: toolkit/audit.md is of another toolkit: the toolkit changed since it was audited.
kbstatus.next.targets: No code repository is set up. `harness-rookie-get-me-ready` sets the target repositories up first.
kbstatus.next.kb_repo: The knowledge base is not a target repository yet, so no task can write it. `harness-rookie-get-me-ready` sets it up (`harness target init-kb` and an entry in target.override.json).
kbstatus.next.toolkit: Next: the toolkit that lets a script read this code (once per code base). Offer `generic-kb-toolkit-design`; after the user approves the design, the user types `/generic-kb-toolkit-build`. The user will be asked for 5 to 10 uses they know ("job X runs procedure Y").
kbstatus.next.map: Next: run `harness kb map`. When facts are missing, or files failed, the toolkit is fixed first (the user types `/generic-kb-toolkit-build`).
kbstatus.next.audit: Next: measure how right the map is before learning from it. Offer `generic-kb-toolkit-audit`.
kbstatus.next.domains: Next: the domains. Offer `generic-kb-domains` (the user confirms the cut once). When the user already knows the domain to learn, go straight to `generic-kb-learn-plan` with its entry points.
kbstatus.next.plan: Next: learn `{domain}`. Offer `generic-kb-learn-plan`: it opens one task for the whole domain, plans its batches, and the user approves the plan once. Ask the user for the entry points, the scope, and any research note or runbook.
kbstatus.next.batch: Next: `{domain}` has {left} objects left in {batches} batches, and no task learns it. Offer `generic-kb-learn-plan`: it opens one task for the rest, from the plan the domain has.
kbstatus.map.empty: The toolkit found nothing in {repos}: another kind of code. Name the repositories the toolkit is for in `repos` of `toolkit.json`, or give that code a toolkit of its own.
kbstatus.next.task_plan: Next: the learn plan of `{domain}` waits in the task `{task}`. The user reads its PLAN.md and approves it in the terminal; then the batches are learned in that task.
kbstatus.next.task_batch: Next: go on learning `{domain}` in the task `{task}`: {left} objects left in {batches} batches. The user says "continue {task}" (a new chat every two or three batches keeps it sharp).
kbstatus.next.task_architecture: Next: every batch of `{domain}` is learned in the task `{task}`. Write its architecture there (`generic-kb-learn-synthesize`), then the whole domain is written back once.
kbstatus.next.task_writeback: Next: `{domain}` is learned in the task `{task}` but not written back. Run the diff and the promote dry-run there; the user approves the write-back in the terminal.
kbstatus.next.maintain: The knowledge base is built. From here it is kept true in daily work, and the user needs no command for it: when code changes, the agent sees which cards went stale and offers to fix them (`generic-kb-refresh`); when a task teaches something, the agent offers to write it in (`generic-capture-knowledge`); when someone answers a row of `requests.md`, the agent writes the answer in. To learn another domain: `generic-kb-learn-plan`.
kbstatus.stop: Before you stop: the knowledge base of this code is not built yet (step {step} of {of}). At the end of your answer, offer the next step to the user in one or two lines, and do not start it: {next} The user can turn this off: `"kb_offer": false` in .harness/policies/task.override.json.
kbaudit.type: No object of type {types} in the map.
kbaudit.sample.next: Read each object's code, blind: fetch its file and read it from `line` for `lines` lines; do not run `kb near` or look at the map for these objects first. Write one line per use you find into a JSON lines file in the task (form: `answer_form`; `{"from": id, "none": true}` for an object that uses nothing), with the line you saw it on. Then `kb audit --answers <file>`.
kbaudit.answers.line: line {line}: not a reading (needs `from`, and `to` or `none`)
kbaudit.score.pass: Every type is at or above the bar. Still look at `map_misses` and `map_only`: each is a use the map gets wrong. Write AUDIT.md and keep it with the toolkit.
kbaudit.score.fail: Below the bar, or lines not read. Check every difference at its line first: a reading that was wrong is fixed in the answers (say so in AUDIT.md), then score again. What is left is the map's: `map_misses` (the toolkit does not see a use) and `map_only` (the toolkit sees one that is not there). Fix the toolkit with /generic-kb-toolkit-build, with these as examples.
kbaudit.score.ambiguous: A reading names a short name that fits several objects (`ambiguous`: the same `schema.name` in two databases, say): it is not scored, and neither is the map's use of it. Look at the line, write the name in full as the code resolves it (the database of the file, or its `USE`), and score again.
kblearn.none: No object in the map is called `{query}`. Run `kb map` again if the code changed.

kblearn.order.next: The plan, by script. kblearn.flows.next: Paths by script: every use the entry point reaches, each on its shortest path. Write the Flows of architecture.md from them: an id for each step, an arrow between steps. `kb cardcheck` checks every flow line against the map.
kblearn.index.next: Lines added and stamped with the sha of the base branch. Next: `kb cardcheck --path` and `kb check --path` on the same folder.
kblearn.index.nothing: Every id is in the index already. To record that a card was checked again, use `kb stamp`.
kblearn.index.unstamped: Lines added, but some have no sha: `unknown_repos` are not set up here (`harness target list`), `gone` are not on the base branch. `kb stale` cannot follow them until they are stamped: set the repository up, or run `kb map` again, then `kb stamp`.
kblearn.check.nowhere: the map has no such use
kblearn.check.left_out: {id} ({file}): {field} leaves out {other}, which the map has
kblearn.check.flow: architecture.md line {line}: {left} and {right} are not linked in the map within {steps} steps
kblearn.check.no_cites: {id} ({file}): {lines} lines of code and no line cited. Cite the lines of each rule (`L120-L145`) so that it can be checked against the code
kblearn.check.few_cites: {id} ({file}): {lines} lines of code and no line cited
kblearn.check.cites_old: {id} ({file}): the card was stamped against older code, so its line numbers were not checked (`kb stale` lists it)
kblearn.check.cite_out: {id} ({file}): {cites} not in its code: {path} lines {low} to {high} on the base branch
kblearn.check.no_objects: No objects/ folder in {folder}: give the domain folder.
kblearn.check.bad: Fix the cards: a relation the map does not have is made up or under the wrong field; one the map has must be written. When the code is right and the map is wrong, fix the toolkit (`kb map`), not the card. `warning_list`: callers left out (allowed) and uses of objects whose SQL is known only at run time.
kblearn.check.ok: The relations of the cards and the flows agree with the map.
kbmap.gaps.inventory: The production list {file} cannot be read: {problem}
kbmap.gaps.no_ids: it holds no id (`type:name`, one per line, or a CSV with an `id` column)
kbmap.gaps.next: `in_production_not_in_repos`: production runs them but no repository has their code. Ask the user who can get the code (scripted from production, or the last version in git under `deleted`). Record each in the knowledge base with `source_missing` and level `unknown`. `in_repos_not_in_production`: not deployed, or retired without being moved to an obsolete folder: ask before calling them dead.
kbmap.gaps.next_no_inventory: These come from the repositories only: `missing` names are used but defined in no file; `deleted` shows where git had them and how to get the last version. What production runs that nothing uses is not seen here: ask the user to export the list of production objects with the toolkit's inventory query, then run `kb gaps --inventory <file>`.
desk.title: {name} · task
desk.unknown: The board lists no task called `{name}`.
desk.subtitle: {kind} · round {round} · opened {created} · last change {updated}
desk.actions.title: Waiting for you
desk.actions.paused.hint: You put this task aside. It is not counted as waiting. Take it up again when you are ready.
desk.wait.stopped: Read what the agent wrote in VS Code and answer it there.
desk.wait.cancelled: You cancelled the last message in VS Code, so the agent stopped. Send it a new message there.
desk.wait.autorun: Read the reason in History. Answer the agent in VS Code, or switch autorun on again.
desk.wait.go-plan: The agent does not know yet: nothing tells it. In VS Code, send it a message, for example:
desk.wait.go-promote: The agent does not know yet: nothing tells it. In VS Code, send it a message, for example:
desk.go.plan: The plan is approved. Go ahead and start.
desk.go.promote: The write-back is approved. Run task promote now.
desk.actions.none.hint: The agent has not stopped since your last message, so it is still working. If VS Code looks idle, answer it there.
desk.actions.closed: The task is closed. To work on it again, ask the agent in VS Code to open it.
desk.hint.approve-plan: Read the plan (tab Plan) first. After you approve, the agent may change files under DEV/; until then it only reads and writes notes.
desk.hint.approve-promote: Read the write-back (tab Changes) first. After you approve, the files go into the target repository on a new branch, not committed: you commit them yourself.
desk.hint.recover: A write-back stopped halfway. This puts the target repository back as it was before it; then the agent can try again.
desk.hint.review-extend: The independent checks are used up. Two more rounds let the reviewer look again after the agent's fixes.
desk.hint.review-waive: Let the task through without passing the checks. You take the responsibility; the task report says so.
desk.hint.autorun-on: The agent works down TODO.md without stopping to ask; it stops for approvals and when it cannot go on. Read TODO.md first.
desk.hint.pause: Put the task aside: the board stops saying it waits for you, and the time aside is not counted against you.
desk.overview.hint: Where the task stands (TASK.md), then what is asked (REQ.md). The agent keeps both up to date.
desk.plan.hint: What the agent will change and how it will check it. You approve it before any file is changed.
desk.log.hint: The decisions and findings of the agent, oldest first.
desk.history.hint: What happened to the task, newest first: approvals, fetches, checks, write-backs, pauses.
desk.missing.task: The agent writes it when the task opens.
desk.missing.req: The agent writes down the requirement as it understands it, and asks you what is unclear.
desk.missing.plan: The agent writes the plan before it changes anything in a repository. A task that changes no repository needs none.
desk.missing.todo: A task of the medium or full tier keeps its steps here.
desk.missing.log: The agent notes its decisions here as it works.
desk.changes.none.hint: Changes appear here when the agent edits files under DEV/ (after you approve the plan).
desk.changes.promote: The write-back, as the last dry run prepared it
desk.changes.promote.hint: This is what goes into the target repository when you approve the write-back.
desk.path.hint: A file of the repository ({path}): open it in VS Code.
desk.cut: Too long to show in full: open the file in VS Code for the rest.
desk.footer: As of {as_of}. The page follows the task by itself while the board runs.
reinstall.from.relative: --from must be the full path of the old copy of the harness. Got: "{path}".
reinstall.from.not_harness: {path} is not a copy of the harness: it has no .harness/registry.json.
reinstall.from.same: {path} is this copy, or holds it, or is inside it. Give the path of the OLD copy, a different folder.
reinstall.from.newer: The old copy is version {old}, newer than this one ({new}). Copying back to an older harness is not supported: update this copy first.
reinstall.nothing: Nothing to copy from {path}: it has no tasks, runtime, overrides or knowledge base of its own.
reinstall.why.exists: already in this copy; not overwritten
reinstall.why.files_exist: {count} file(s) already in this copy; not overwritten
reinstall.why.kb_has_content: this copy's knowledge base already has content; not merged. Empty it first if the old one should replace it
reinstall.why.not_git: cannot tell whether the company changed it: the old copy is not a git repository
reinstall.why.both_changed: changed in the old copy and in this one; compare them by hand
reinstall.next.dry: Nothing was copied. Show this to the user: what would be copied, what is skipped and why, and the files changed in the old copy that are not carried. Then ask the user to close the VS Code windows of the old copy and run the same command with --apply in their own terminal.
reinstall.person.dry: Nothing was copied. Close the VS Code windows of the old copy, then run the same command with --apply.
reinstall.next.done: Copied; the old copy is not changed. Check `checked`: every doctor [ERROR] must be fixed. When doctor warns that the short command points at another copy, redo step 1 of /harness-rookie-get-me-ready. A new chat is a new session: it must run `task open <name>` to go on with a task; only an old chat finds its task by itself. Delete the old copy only when the user has seen that all works.
reinstall.next.failed: Some items could not be copied (see `failed`). Fix the cause, then run the same command again: what was copied is skipped, the rest goes over.
task.handoff.env: Give the environment with --env: a short name such as DEV, up to {limit} characters.
task.handoff.next: The board now says the task waits for the user's test results. Tell the user to open TEST-GUIDE.md on the task's page (the Test tab), run the tests, and bring the results back here. Then stop. When they do, run `{command} task handoff clear` first.
task.handoff.none: Task {name} has no handoff to clear.
task.handoff.cleared: The mark is gone. Save the results as the user gave them, judge them against the pass criteria, then update the task files.
promote.done.test_offer: The next step is testing in the environments (DEV, IST, QAT). Offer the user a test task with the skill `generic-test-guide` (it asks first).
desk.wait.tests: Run the tests in TEST-GUIDE.md (the Test tab) in the environment named, then bring the results back to the agent in VS Code. A message such as:
desk.tests.prompt: Here are the test results: (paste the output, numbers and anything unexpected).
task.name.shell: The task name `{name}` has {chars}: a terminal reads it as a command, a quote, a variable or a wildcard, and the task name is typed in every command. Use letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, and do not start with `-`. For example: `{example}`.
doctor.task_names: A task folder has characters in its name that a terminal reads as commands: {names}. It still opens, but its commands need quotes, and on Windows cmd `&` and `^` break them. Rename the folder, or make the task again under a safe name.
desk.review.hint: The independent checks of this task: what each reviewer was given, and what it answered, as saved by the harness. The agent cannot change an answer.
desk.review.sum: {n} check(s) in a row asked · {passes} passed on the version as it is now · {used} of {limit} used
desk.review.off: No check is asked for; the rounds below ran earlier.
desk.review.none: Checks are on, but none has run yet.
desk.review.noanswer: The answer file is not there.
desk.review.pending: The reviewer has not answered yet.
desk.review.earlier: an earlier version of the work
stage.again: The last round was written back, or the requirement changed: the plan is asked for again.
board.lobby.quiet: The lab is quiet. Every task is closed. Say what you want done in VS Code.
desk.actions.quiet: No sign of the agent for a while
desk.actions.quiet.hint: A session holds this task, but it has done nothing for a few minutes and has not stopped. A long step may be running, or the VS Code window may be closed. If it is closed, open a session and say the task name.
desk.actions.unheld.hint: The session that had it moved on to another task, or is gone. Nothing happens until you open a session and ask for the task by name.
desk.unheld.note: No session holds this task. When you have decided, open a session in VS Code and ask for the task by name.
task.busy: The agent is in the middle of a turn on this task (a session holds it, called a tool in the last {minutes} min and has not stopped). It may be answering a doubt about the result, or still changing it. `{command}` waits until it has stopped. Stop it in VS Code, or add --force.
serve.busy: The agent is at work on this task. It may be answering you. Nothing here works until it has stopped; then decide.
board.action.busy: The agent is at work. Decide once it has stopped.
desk.busy.note: The agent is at work on this task, and may be answering a question about the result. Nothing here can be pressed until it has stopped: then approve, or ask again. To stop it now, use the stop button in VS Code.
board.close.quiet: The agent made no call for 5 minutes and has not stopped. It may still be running a long step. Close the task only if it is not.
desk.test.hint: The test guide the agent wrote for you, then each environment with the results file and the verdict the agent judged. Run the tests, then bring the results back to the agent in VS Code.
desk.test.noguide: The agent has not written TEST-GUIDE.md yet.
desk.test.waiting: Run the tests of {env} in TEST-GUIDE.md and bring the results back to the agent in VS Code.
task.defects.odd: A defect heading is not in the form `## D<n> [open] <environment>: <title>`: {line}. Its status cannot be told.
task.defects.by_hand: {id} was marked fixed by hand, but {env} has not passed: it is open again. Only `task defects sync` marks a defect fixed, when the results of the environment say PASS.
